title: Session revocation updates refresh tokens without checking session ownership

original_titles.title: DELETE /me/sessions/{id} revokes another user's refresh tokens (IDOR)

problem: DELETE /v1/me/sessions/{session_id} correctly scopes the app.sessions update by both session_id and principal.id, but the following refresh-token UPDATE filters only by session_id. If an attacker obtains another user’s session UUID, the second statement can revoke that user’s refresh-token family even though the session-row ownership update matched nothing.
impact: This permits cross-user session disruption/logout. It is not necessarily account takeover, but it is an authorization failure and can invalidate a victim’s refresh tokens.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Select/lock the session row using both id and user_id = principal.id. If no row is found, return the same 404/204 policy without touching refresh tokens.
Update refresh tokens with an ownership predicate as well: join refresh_tokens to sessions and require sessions.user_id = principal.id, or store and verify user_id directly on refresh_tokens.
Check the row count and write an audit event only when an owned session was revoked. Do not reveal whether another user’s session id exists.

Add a two-user test: user A tries to revoke user B’s session id; verify B’s session remains active and all B refresh tokens are unchanged. Then verify A can revoke A’s own session and its refresh tokens.

acceptance_criteria: Cross-user session revocation changes zero rows in both sessions and refresh_tokens.
Own-session revocation updates both tables atomically.
A 404/non-disclosing response is returned for foreign session ids.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
